proposals.evidence: Turner 10452 explicitly lists European Romani ǰal 'goes' from yā́ti. The source specifically identifies Zargari džejipej 'to go' as an irregular infinitive from džā- (§3.17.3.2, p. 142), distinguishing this present stem from the gatá-derived irregular past linked in pass100. The infinitive formation is source morphology, not a separate etymon. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

proposals.evidence: Turner 5055 explicitly lists European Romani čiv- 'to throw, put' in its section crossed with kṣipáti. The source prints Zargari čuv [čuw] 'Throw!' in §2.3.20 (p. 128), while giving final /v/ > [w]. The i/u vowel difference is retained as a local form, not explained by an invented sound rule. This short imperative is assigned to the attested Romani branch with Turner's crossing retained in the note, not to a bare kṣipáti node. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.
